foetal movement.d: motion of a fetus within the uterus (usually detected by the 16th week of pregnancy)

foetal monitor.d: an electronic monitor that monitors fetal heartbeat and the mother's uterine contractions during childbirth

foetal circulation.d: the system of blood vessels and structures through which blood moves in a fetus

foetal distress.d: an abnormal condition of a fetus; usually discovered during pregnancy and characterized by an abnormal heart rhythm

foe.d: an armed adversary (especially a member of an opposing military force)

foetor.d: a distinctive odor that is offensively unpleasant

foetal.d: of or relating to a fetus

foetology.d: the branch of medicine concerned with the fetus in the uterus

foetus.d: an unborn or unhatched vertebrate in the later stages of development showing the main recognizable features of the mature animal

foetoprotein.d: any of several antigens that occur naturally in the fetus and sometimes in adults with cancer

foeman.d: an armed adversary (especially a member of an opposing military force)

foeniculum.d: very small genus of aromatic European herbs with pinnately compound leaves and yellow flowers

foehn.d: a warm dry wind that blows down the northern slopes of the Alps

foetoscopy.d: prenatal diagnosis that allows direct observation of a fetus in the uterus and the withdrawal of fetal blood

foetometry.d: measurement of a fetus (especially the diameter of the head)

foetoscope.d: a stethoscope placed on the pregnant woman's abdomen to listen for the fetal heartbeat

foetid pothos.d: deciduous perennial low-growing fetid swamp plant of eastern North America having minute flowers enclosed in a mottled greenish or purple cowl-shaped spathe

foetid bugbane.d: bugbane of Siberia and eastern Asia having ill-smelling green-white flowers
